newsitem.title: FRANCE: Polisario warns of war if U.N. fails in W.Sahara.
newsitem.headline: Polisario warns of war if U.N. fails in W.Sahara.

text.p: The Polisario Front, which seeks an independent state in the Western Sahara mainly controlled by Morocco, warned on Sunday it would resume war if the United Nations failed to implement its delayed peace plan.
"In the case of a U.N. failure, the solution lies in resuming the war," Polisario's leader Mohamed Abdelaziz told the official Algerian agency APS on Sunday.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Friday he was studying whether a long-stalled U.N. peace plan for the disputed territory could still be carried out, or whether it could be modified or some different solution found.
Abdelaziz said Polisario pinned great hope on Annan to hold a U.N.-sponsored referendum which should have been held in January 1992.
The ballot would decide whether Western Sahara, a former Spanish colony, should be incorporated into Morocco or become independent as sought by Polisario.
Continuing differences between Morocco and Polisario over who should vote in the referendum have stymied the plan.
"In the event of the United Nations failing, we see no other way out than defending our national rights by every means, in particular through armed struggle," said Abdelaziz.
The two sides hav been observing a ceasefire since September 1991, monitored by a U.N. observer force.
